analyst_view.overall: Early view: PSG host Lorient three days after facing Roma in the Champions League, and Dembele, Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes and Kvaratskhelia were all injured as of early November. Lorient (10th) are built on defence: eight goals conceded in 10 games and clean sheets in most of their away games, including 2-0 at Le Havre.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean lower: Alexandre Dujeux's Lorient defend deep and have conceded only eight, and PSG were held to 1-0 by a similar low block from Troyes. With Roma midweek and key attackers out, a 2-0 type win is the most natural outcome.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners. I stay with that: PSG average 5.5 corners and should get more against a side that sits deep, while Lorient win only 3.7 (15th). It hinges on how much PSG rotate after Roma.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.8 cards. That already reflects two of the cleanest teams in the league: PSG commit the fewest fouls (6.5 a game) and Lorient are 17th (9.3). I see nothing to move it either way.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots. Season figures (PSG 19.3, Lorient 10.3) support that, so I stay put. Lorient rarely shoot, so nearly all of the total depends on PSG's line-up after Roma.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target. I lean lower: Lorient are last in the league for shots on target (2.8 a game), and their deep defending blocks many efforts; PSG had seven on target against Troyes. Nine or ten looks more realistic.
